steps.body: Every hundredths decimal converts back to a fraction over 100: 0.43 is 43/100.
steps.narration: Every hundredths decimal converts back to a fraction over 100: 0.43 is 43/100.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.43. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades only 3 single cells. The tenths digit of 0.43 is worth whole columns: 4 full columns first, then 3 more cells.
That count swaps the digits of 0.43. The first digit after the point counts full columns; the second counts single cells.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 43 of the 100 cells — 4 full columns and 3 more cells: 43 hundredths, written 0.43.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: You will shade 0.43. Which fraction names the same amount?
predict.reveal: 0.43 is 43 hundredths — 43 of 100 equal parts. Swapping the digits to 34/100 would name a different shading, and 43/10 would be more than four whole grids — tenths are ten times bigger pieces than hundredths.

explanationVariants: The digits end in the hundredths place, so the fraction is 43/100.

widget.prompt: Which fraction names the same amount as 0.43?

options.feedback: A denominator of 10 makes this 43 tenths — more than one whole. The two digits of 0.43 end in the hundredths place, so the whole names hundredths.
That keeps only the tenths digit and drops the hundredths digit entirely. Both decimal digits of 0.43 count toward the amount: 43 hundredths in all.
That fraction swaps the two digits of 0.43. Read the decimal place by place — the digit order carries the value.
Correct — the digits of 0.43 end in the hundredths place, so the amount is 43 out of 100 equal parts.
